citations.assessment: The two-stage transmission is explicit in the Song of Songs midrash: Simon reports from Yonatan of Beit Guvrin who reports from Yehoshua ben Levi.
The current digital division places the quoted Simon attribution in halakhah 3, within the clothing discussion. Preserve the received locator as well.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The Song of Songs midrash explicitly has Simon in the name of Yonatan of Beit Guvrin in this verse exposition.
This verse exposition has Simon in Natan of Beit Guvrin’s name and compares birth and emergence from Sheol.
The parallel gives bare Yonatan reporting in the name of Yonatan of Beit Guvrin.
The first Yonatan is the transmitting voice and the place-designated Yonatan is the immediate source.
The Metzora passage has a distinct Yaakov–Yehudah–Natan chain and uses Natan of Beit Guvrin.

holds.reason: The competing midrash readings support Heilprin’s comparison but do not prove a copying error in all occurrences. Preserve the specific proposal and the final Natan chain.
